criteriaNow.text: When someone runs `structure-sweep move apply` on a plan of many rows where a few rows move a file into another workspace package, the command stops before writing anything, names each cross-package row and the package it would enter, and leaves every file and manifest unchanged
When someone runs the command on a single row that moves a file into another package, the command refuses, saying the move crosses packages and that such moves are not supported yet
When someone runs the command on a single row that moves a file into another package, the file is still at its old path afterwards
When someone runs the command on a plan whose rows all stay inside one package, the moves are applied as before, so existing single-package behaviour is unchanged

When someone runs `structure-sweep move apply` with a plan that moves files into other workspace packages, then runs the workspace build, every moved file's importers resolve through the target package's exports, the `workspace:*` dependency is in the importing package's manifest, the lockfile match
When someone moves a file into another package and reads the importing package's manifest, the importing package lists the target as a `workspace:*` dependency
When someone moves a file into another package and reads the moved file's importers, the imports name the target package, not a relative path into it
When someone moves a file into another package and the target package does not export that file, the move is refused with a message saying the file must be exported first
When someone moves a file into another package and the target package does not export that file, nothing is written to the workspace
When someone's plan contains a row that would make two packages depend on each other, that row is refused with the cycle named
When someone's plan contains a row that would make two packages depend on each other, the other rows in the plan are not applied either
When someone applies a cross-package move and the lockfile is regenerated, the lockfile gains the new workspace:* link
When someone applies a cross-package move and the lockfile is regenerated, no unrelated lockfile entries change

When someone runs `structure-sweep move apply` with a plan that moves files into other workspace packages, then runs the workspace build, the move is either refused with a reason or completed with importers resolving through exports, the `workspace:*` dependency present, the lockfile matching it, an
When someone looks at the importing package after a cross-package move completes, its imports read as package names, not relative paths into the other package
A test that applies a plan with a cross-package row and asserts the refusal, the named rows, and no change, plus one asserting a single-package plan still returns without error
A test that fails if a same-package move is not performed, checking that the file is actually moved
A manifest that cannot be read is reported as a problem and the move is refused, so cycle detection never runs on an incomplete graph
A missing lockfile or importer block is reported and the move is refused before anything is written, or the lockfile is created or updated so it matches the manifest
Importers of a same-package move are rewritten to the new relative path, and the test checks an importer after the move so it fails if they are not
A source package whose manifest cannot be read is reported as a problem and the move is refused, rather than being silently skipped
